# Menu keyboard focus falls to the body when a level holding it closes

## Context

The operator asked for more tests of menu hover and keyboard navigation, submenus included (2026-09-18). Scratch Playwright arms against `dev@3f859a4803` found that keyboard focus falls to the `<body>` whenever a menu level that holds focus closes, except through Left or Escape inside a submenu. The runs used the component app `test/playwright/component/apps/empty-viewport`: a floating `menu.List`, and a `button.Base` with a `menu`, both carrying a three-level tree.

| scenario | `document.activeElement` after | menu | then Escape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Right into a submenu, pointer rests on a root **leaf** | `body` | root stays open | nothing happens |
| Right into a submenu, pointer rests on **another root parent** | `body` | the new preview opens | — |
| focus at depth 3, pointer rests on a depth-2 leaf | `body` | two levels stay | — |
| button menu: row 1 | `body` | stays open | nothing happens |
| button menu: Right into a submenu, then Enter / Space / click on a leaf | `body` (expected: the button) | closes | — |
| button menu: Right, Left back to the root, then Escape (or Enter on a root leaf) | `body` (expected: the button) | closes | — |
| CONTROL, button menu: no submenu visit (a focus-rest preview only), then Escape | the button ✓ | closes | — |

## The Problem

- **`component.Base#revertFocus()`** (`src/component/Base.mjs:1872-1878`) is the only hand-back when a component that holds focus unmounts. It focuses `Neo.getComponent(focusEnterData.relatedTarget.id)`, and only while `containsFocus` is set.
- **Every level is its own focus branch.** A submenu is created with the root's `parentComponent` and `parentId: app.mainView.id` (`src/menu/List.mjs:893-894`), so `manager.Focus` sees each level separately. Moving into a submenu raises `focusLeave` on the parent level, and `component.Base#onFocusLeave` clears its `focusEnterData`. Moving back re-enters with the submenu item as `relatedTarget`, which is a node id, not a component.
- **A partial close has nothing to revert to.** When a level unmounts while it holds focus, its `relatedTarget` is the parent's item node. `getComponent()` finds nothing and focus lands on the body.
- **A full close has lost its source.** Once focus has visited any submenu, the root no longer knows its entry source (the trigger), so no dismissal can return focus to it.
- **The damage.** With focus on the body, the root stays open, because its `menuFocus` never saw a leave. The Navigator's keydown listener sits on the menu element, so arrows and Escape are dead until an outside click.
- **The one path that works** is `leaveSubMenu()` (Left, or Escape inside a submenu). It focuses the parent item *before* it hides the level (`src/menu/List.mjs:557-567`). The pointer-rest paths (`onItemRest` → `hideSubMenu()`, or `showSubMenu()` switching siblings) and the cascade dismissals do not.

## The Architectural Reality

- `menu.List` treats a cascade as one interaction island for pointer dismissal (`isInteractionPath`, `onFocusLeave`). Focus hand-back is the one island behaviour it leaves to the per-component `revertFocus()`.
- `onFocusMove`'s JSDoc depends on the levels being separate branches: a move into a submenu must never reach the parent menu's `onFocusMove`. That rules out re-parenting the levels, so the hand-back belongs in `menu.List`.

## The Fix

`src/menu/List.mjs`:

1. **Partial close.** `hideSubMenu()` hands focus to the item that opened the branch before it unmounts it, whenever that branch holds focus and this level stays. "The branch holds focus" means some level on the `activeSubMenu` chain has `containsFocus`. `leaveSubMenu()` then reduces to asking its parent to hide it, because its focus step moves into the shared path. A level hiding its branch inside its own `unmount()` does not hand focus back, since the level itself is leaving. `unmount()` says so explicitly, the way `showSubMenu()` takes a `focus` flag.
2. **Full close.** The root remembers where focus entered the cascade from: the first focus enter after mount. When it unmounts with focus anywhere in the cascade, it returns focus there. This replaces the inherited `revertFocus()`, which cannot see across levels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With focus in a submenu, a pointer rest on a root leaf, or on another root parent, puts focus on the item that opened the closed level. Arrows and Escape then work.
- [ ] With focus at depth 3, a rest on a depth-2 leaf puts focus on the depth-2 parent item.
- [ ] Button menu: a leaf chosen at depth 2 by Enter, Space or click returns focus to the button. After Right and Left, Escape returns focus to the button.
- [ ] Controls, unchanged: with no submenu visit, Escape returns focus to the button. Left or Escape inside a submenu still closes that level and focuses its parent item.
- [ ] Each defect arm fails first on `dev`. The arms live in `test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs`, with the button-menu arms beside the existing ones in `test/playwright/component/button/Base.spec.mjs`.

## Out of Scope

- A pointer rest moving keyboard focus. A rest stays a preview (#18759). Focus moves only because its host is closing.
- Keys typed while a submenu mount is still in flight. Two fast Right presses land on depth 2, not 3. That is a separate, unfiled observation.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-parenting submenus (`parentComponent: me`)** so `manager.Focus` sees one island. Item-to-submenu moves would then reach the parent's `onFocusMove`, which resolves rows against its own store.
- **Keying "this level stays" on `mounted`.** `unmount()` hides the branch before `super.unmount()`, so a closing level still reads as mounted while its own cascade runs.
- **Refocusing from a timer after the removal.** The class contract is structural: "timing is never the ownership signal".
